ety.text: From Ancient Greek νεῦρον (neûron, “a sinew, nerve”) + -al.

senses.d: Of, or relating to the nerves, neurons or the nervous system.
Modelled on the arrangement of neurons in the brain.

grp.label: of or relating to the nerves

ety.text: From Middle French neutral (compare modern French neutre), from Latin neutrālis. By surface analysis, neuter + -al.

senses.d: Not taking sides in a conflict such as war; nonaligned.
Favoring neither the supporting nor opposing viewpoint of a topic of debate; unbiased.
ex: I am neutral regarding the issue of gay marriage.
The heart can not possibly remain neutral, but constantly takes part one way or the other.

senses.d: Neither positive nor negative.
Not biased; viewing situations objectively in a way that is neither positive nor negative.
Neither beneficial nor harmful.
ex:
Some things good, and some things ill, do seem,
 And neutral some, in her fantastic eye.

senses.d: Having no sex; neuter.
Having no obvious colour; gray.
Neither positive nor negative; possessing no charge or equivalent positive and negative charge such that there is no imbalance.
Having a pH of or near 7, neither acidic nor alkaline.
Of an alcoholic drink, having been fermented and distilled but with no additives.
A nonaligned state, or a member of such a state.
A person who takes no side in a dispute.
ex:
They say in Harlan County
 There are no neutrals there
 You'll either be a union man
 Or a thug for J.H. Blair.

senses.d: An individual or entity serving as an arbitrator or adjudicator.
A neutral hue.
The position of a set of gears in which power cannot be transmitted to the drive mechanism.
ex: Put it in neutral, and we'll push it out of the garage.

senses.d: An electrical terminal or conductor which has zero or close to zero voltage with respect to the ground.

grp.label: not taking sides in a conflict

ety.text: Inherited from Old French neutre, from Latin neuter.

pt:neutro.gl: neutral (not taking sides in a conflict such as war)

es:neutro.gl: neuter (neither the one thing nor the other)

pt:ponto morto.gl: neutral (gear position in which power cannot be transmitted to the drive mechanism)

ety.text: From Middle French neutralité, from Medieval Latin neutralitas. Morphologically neutral + -ity.

senses.d: The state or quality of being neutral; the condition of being unengaged in contests between others; state of taking no part on either side.
ex: Men who possess a state of neutrality in times of public danger, desert the interest of their fellow subjects.
The official pretence of a scrupulous solicitude to maintain neutrality is flagrantly insincere.

senses.d: Indifference in quality; a state neither very good nor bad.
ex:
There is no health; physicians say that we
At best enjoy but a neutrality.

senses.d: The quality or state of being neutral.
The condition of a nation or government which refrains from taking part, directly or indirectly, in a war between other powers.
Those who are neutral; a combination of neutral powers or states.

grp.label: state of being neutral; taking no part on either side
